title: Identity, errors and delivery guarantees
summary: Service allowlisting and protocol parsing are insufficient authentication. Before an inbound operation, the server must derive trusted caller identity and authorization context from an authenticated connection/policy, apply admission and resource limits, then call the dispatcher. Protocol faults must be sanitized and retain precise protocol-specific status semantics.
invariants: Untrusted payload may supply requested published operation and data, not target receiver/method or authorization context.
TLS identity, token verification, permissions and tenant scope are dedicated policy mechanisms, not inferred by codec or registry presence.
Post-send uncertain outcomes must not trigger automatic retries for effectful operations.
Queue Fabric durability/ack/recovery is not silently conferred on JSON-RPC, SOAP or gRPC streams.
Deadlines use bounded time accounting and must not be confused with proof that work stopped on the remote peer.
